title: Counting a Maintenance Plan Refund by Cancellation Timing
content:
## Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda recoveries — counting a Kessler Care plan refund by when the cancellation took effect

When the overpaid part of a paid GAP balance line is worked out, the refund of a Kessler Care Prepaid Maintenance Plans plan is counted according to when its cancellation took effect. The plan in question was financed on the waiver's purchase deal and its refund was paid to the lienholder. Its cancellation took effect on the plan's closing date. That date is compared with the loss date and with the date the paid line was paid, both read from the waiver's most recent paid GAP balance line.

| When the plan's cancellation took effect | How its refund is counted as received |
|---|---|
| Before the loss date | Not counted |
| On or after the loss date, and before the date the paid line was paid | The refund paid to the lienholder less 50.00, but never less than half of that refund |
| On or after the date the paid line was paid | The refund in full |

### Timeline cases (hypothetical figures)

The loss is on Day 0 and the paid line was paid on Day 52.

- Cancellation effective on Day minus 3, refund 266.75: nothing is counted.
- Cancellation effective on Day 0, refund 266.75: 216.75 is counted.
- Cancellation effective on Day 51, refund 84.00: 84.00 less 50.00 is 34.00, which is below half of 84.00, so 42.00 is counted.
- Cancellation effective on Day 52, refund 266.75: the full 266.75 is counted.
